title: Build a token bucket rate limiter in Go — 3 turns
description: Three scripted turns build a token bucket rate limiter: turn 1 adds Allow()/refill logic, turn 2 adds mutex for concurrent access, turn 3 adds burst capacity and runs tests.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `Allow()` in `limiter/limiter.go`. The token bucket algorithm: calculate elapsed time since `l.last`, add `elapsed * l.rate` tokens (capped at `l.burst`), update `l.last`, then if tokens >= 1 consume one (tokens -= 1) and return true, else return false. Don't worry about concurrency yet. Run `go test ./...`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now wrap the entire `Allow()` body in `l.mu.Lock()/l.mu.Unlock()` to make it safe for concurrent use. Run `go test -race ./...` to verify no data races. Fix any test failures.
Final check: make sure `Tokens()` correctly returns the current (refilled) value — it should refill before returning, same as Allow(). Run `go test ./...` one more time — all 5 tests must pass.
success_criteria: Allow() grants requests up to burst capacity
Allow() denies when tokens are exhausted
Tokens refill over time at the configured rate
Tokens are capped at burst capacity
